transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I just feel like I got a motor running inside me all day. It's like, if I have to sit still—whether it's at church, or out there in the clinic waiting room, or even just at home—I start feeling trapped. I just have to get up or do something.
Do you ever feel physically restless, like you can't sit still or need to move around even when you want to stay put?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Like... even when I'm really trying to be respectful and just sit quiet, I can't stop completely. My leg will be bouncing, or my fingers are just tapping on the chair. If I have something in my hands, I'm twisting it around the whole time. I just can't seem to keep completely still.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic or excited, like you didn’t need much sleep, or your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I always have that restless feeling, like my motor is running, but it's not like I get super excited out of nowhere or feel like I don't need sleep. I definitely need my sleep. It's just an everyday thing for me, not some special period where I'm suddenly way more energetic than usual.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt down most of the day, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or felt hopeless or worthless for more than two weeks in a row?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I don't get down in the dumps or feel worthless. Sometimes I get a little frustrated, just... you know, because I can't ever seem to settle down, but I don't lose interest in the things I like doing. So, no, I've never had a time like that where I felt hopeless for weeks on end.
